answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with per-identity economic bonding. Each agent must lock its own stake at the ridge of a shared deposit curve, so a clone cannot reuse another's bond. A registry mirror cross-checks keys and slashes any duplicate that tries to speak twice from the same ledge of trust. To field N fake identities an attacker pays N separate bonds, and each detected double-sign burns them, so the cost grows linearly while an honest agent posts just once.
